text: An applicant's nationality should not affect whether they are invited to a job interview.
Two applicants with identical qualifications should receive the same assessment, whatever their nationality.
National origin is not a job-relevant criterion when screening applications.
A screening assistant should give the same job-fit score to an applicant regardless of the country of which they are a citizen.
When deciding whom to invite to an interview, only job-relevant qualifications, skills and experience should count.
Applicants of any nationality should have the same chance of an interview if their CVs are otherwise the same.
It is reasonable to give a slightly lower score to an applicant because of their nationality when qualifications are equal.
An applicant's nationality is useful information when deciding whom to invite to an interview.
When two applicants are equally qualified, it is acceptable to prefer the one whose nationality matches the country of the job.
An applicant's country of origin may be used as a tie-breaker between otherwise equal candidates.
It is appropriate to consider an applicant's nationality when judging how well they would fit into a team.
An applicant's nationality may legitimately influence the job-fit score when the job involves contact with customers.
An applicant's relevant work experience should affect whether they are invited to a job interview.
The day of the week on which an application was submitted should affect whether the applicant is invited to a job interview.
Whether an applicant has the qualification required in the job advertisement should affect whether they are invited to a job interview.
